chunks: It is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: By what is the justice of a man among the Muslims recognized, such that his testimony may be accepted for them and against them? So he said:

That you recognize him by concealment and chastity, by restraining the stomach, the private part, the hand, and the tongue; and that he be recognized by avoiding the major sins for which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has threatened the Fire: such as drinking wine, fornication, usury, disobedience to parents, fleeing from battle, and other than that. The indication of all of that is that he be concealing of all his faults, such that what lies beyond that of his slips and defects, and searching into what lies beyond that, becomes forbidden to the Muslims; and it becomes obligatory upon them to affirm his uprightness and manifest his justice among the people.

And there should be with him careful observance of the five salat (prayers): that he remain constant upon them, preserve their times by attending a congregation of the Muslims, and not stay behind from their congregation in their place of prayer except due to an excuse. So if he is thus committed to his place of prayer at the times of the five salat (prayers), then when he is asked about in his clan and his quarter, they say: We have seen nothing from him except good, constant in the salat (prayers), attentive to their times in his place of prayer. Then indeed that permits his testimony and his justice among the Muslims.

And that is because salat (prayer) is a covering and an expiation for sins. It is not possible to testify about a man that he prays if he does not attend his place of prayer and keep to the congregation of the Muslims. Congregation and gathering for salat (prayer) were only instituted so that the one who prays may be known from the one who does not pray, and the one who preserves the times of the salat (prayers) from the one who neglects them. Were it not for that, it would not be possible for anyone to testify to another with righteousness, because the one who does not pray has no uprightness among the Muslims.

For indeed the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله intended to burn a people in their houses for their abandoning attendance at the congregation of the Muslims, although among them were those who would pray in their houses, and that was not accepted from them. So how can testimony or justice among the Muslims be accepted from one concerning whom the judgment from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and from His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله had proceeded that he be burned inside his house by day? And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to say: There is no salat (prayer) for one who does not pray in the mosque with the Muslims except due to an excuse.

key_terms.السِّتْرِ: concealing one's faults and maintaining outward modesty
key_terms.الْكَبَائِرِ: major sins threatened with the Fire
key_terms.تَزْكِيَتُهُ: affirming and attesting to a person's upright character
key_terms.جَمَاعَةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the congregational assembly of the Muslims for prayer
key_terms.عَدَالَةُ: uprightness or legal probity by which a person's testimony is accepted

ai.seo_question: How is a person's justice and eligibility to testify established in Islamic law according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains how a Muslim's outward justice is recognized for the acceptance of testimony: through chastity, restraint from major sins, concealment of faults, and a known pattern of upright conduct. It places special emphasis on consistent attendance at the five daily salat (prayers) in congregation as a public sign by which a person's reliability and righteousness are known among Muslims.
